SELECTED_INDEX: 2
CONFIDENCE: 0.46
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the typical pattern of a para-disubstituted benzene:  
• Very strong C–H out-of-plane doublet 805 / 818 cm⁻¹ and ring breathing at 1003 cm⁻¹ – characteristic of 1,4-disubstitution.  
• Aromatic C=C stretch 1608 cm⁻¹ and multiple aromatic C–H stretches 3013/3073 cm⁻¹ are present.  
• A single strong C=O stretch at 1682 cm⁻¹ indicates one conjugated carbonyl (aryl-CO-) as in an acetophenone; its position is lowered from 1715 to ~1685 cm⁻¹ by conjugation, matching an acyl group directly on the ring.  
• Intense 1075 cm⁻¹ and 1269 cm⁻¹ bands fit CH₃ rocking/umbrella and C–CH₃ bends expected for a para-methyl substituent.  
Among the candidates, only 2 (CC(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1, p-methylacetophenone) possesses exactly a para acetyl and methyl on an aromatic ring, giving the required 1,4-disubstitution and a conjugated ketone C=O. Other candidates are ortho/meta substituted, non-aromatic, or contain additional hetero groups whose diagnostic Raman bands (e.g., OH, SO, N=N) are absent. Consequently, candidate 2 best matches the observed Raman features.
